title: Test patterns (any URL)
summary: The standard test shapes: smoke, average load, stress, spike, breakpoint and soak. Includes an enterprise test plan (jobs starting ent-).
description: The standard test shapes against any URL: a smoke test, average load, a stress ramp to four times normal, a sudden spike, a breakpoint ramp that runs until the target breaks, a 30-minute soak and a maximum-throughput run. Start here if you are new to load testing.

variables.name: url
variables.guide: The address of the system to test, starting with https:// (or http://) and with no trailing slash, for example https://staging.example.com. Use a system you own, ideally a staging copy. BLASTA runs in a container, so for a service on your own machine use host.docker.internal instead of localhost.

variables.name: path
variables.description: Path to test, starting with /. Pick a representative page or endpoint.
variables.guide:
The part of the address after the domain, starting with /, for example /pricing or /api/health.
Pick a page that is typical of real traffic: the home page is often cached and flatters the result.

jobs.name: smoke test
jobs.notes: One request a second for 30 seconds. Run this first: it proves the target, path and headers are right before you apply real load.

job.name: smoke test

jobs.name: average load (5 min)
jobs.notes: Your normal traffic. Set rps to what production sees at a typical hour; the p95 here is your baseline to compare other runs against.

job.name: average load (5 min)

jobs.name: stress ramp to 4x
jobs.notes: Ramps to 4x average over 5 minutes. Finds where latency starts to climb and which error shows up first (timeouts, 502/503, resets).

job.name: stress ramp to 4x

jobs.name: spike (sudden 10x)
jobs.notes: Reaches 10x average in 10 seconds, then holds. Models a newsletter, a link on social media or a failover. Watch recovery after it ends, not only the peak.

job.name: spike (sudden 10x)

jobs.name: breakpoint (ramp until it breaks)
jobs.notes: Slow ramp to a very high rate over 10 minutes. Stop it when errors pass a few percent: the rate at that moment is your ceiling. Staging only.

job.name: breakpoint (ramp until it breaks)

jobs.name: soak (30 min)
jobs.notes: Moderate steady load for half an hour. Surfaces leaks and slow decay (memory, connections, disk, cache churn) that short runs never reach.

job.name: soak (30 min)

jobs.name: max throughput (closed loop)
jobs.notes: No rate limit: every worker sends as fast as the target answers. Measures raw capacity, but is not realistic traffic, so do not use it for latency SLOs.

job.name: max throughput (closed loop)

jobs.name: Test patterns (any URL): 01 smoke
jobs.notes: Enterprise plan, step 1 of 10. One request a second for 30 seconds. Run this first, every time: it proves the address, credentials and headers are right and that the environment is up before any real load is applied. Gate: zero errors. Reference request: average load (5 min).

job.name: Test patterns (any URL): 01 smoke

jobs.name: Test patterns (any URL): 02 baseline (20% load)
jobs.notes: Step 2 of 10. About a fifth of normal traffic for 5 minutes: the uncontended latency of this request. Every later result is judged against it, so record p50 and p95. Gate: at most 0.5% errors and the default latency targets. Reference request: average load (5 min).

job.name: Test patterns (any URL): 02 baseline (20% load)

jobs.name: Test patterns (any URL): 03 average load (SLO check)
jobs.notes: Step 3 of 10. Normal busy-hour traffic for 10 minutes. The rate is the reference job's rate: raise it to your measured production peak-hour rate. This is the run that proves (or breaks) your SLO. Gate: at most 1% errors, p95 and p99 inside the targets. Reference request: average load (5 min).

job.name: Test patterns (any URL): 03 average load (SLO check)

jobs.name: Test patterns (any URL): 04 peak load (2x average)
jobs.notes: Step 4 of 10. Twice the average for 10 minutes: the busiest hour of the year plus headroom. Latency may rise, but must stay in SLO; if it does not, you have no headroom. Gate: at most 2% errors, latency targets doubled. Reference request: average load (5 min).

job.name: Test patterns (any URL): 04 peak load (2x average)

jobs.name: Test patterns (any URL): 05 stress (ramp to 4x)
jobs.notes: Step 5 of 10. Ramps to four times average over 10 minutes, then holds for 2. Finds where it degrades and HOW: gracefully (latency rises, errors stay low) or badly (errors, timeouts, crashes, restarts). Observation only, no gate. Reference request: average load (5 min).

job.name: Test patterns (any URL): 05 stress (ramp to 4x)

jobs.name: Test patterns (any URL): 06 spike (10x in 10 s)
jobs.notes: Step 6 of 10. Reaches ten times average within 10 seconds and holds for 2 minutes: a campaign email, a news link, a failover. Checks autoscaling, queue limits and load shedding. Gate: at most 5% errors, because shedding load is acceptable and crashing is not. Reference request: average load (5 min).

job.name: Test patterns (any URL): 06 spike (10x in 10 s)

jobs.name: Test patterns (any URL): 07 recovery after the spike
jobs.notes: Step 7 of 10. Run IMMEDIATELY after the spike, at average load for 5 minutes. Latency and errors must return to the baseline from step 2. If they do not, something is stuck: queues, connection pools, GC, an autoscaler cool-down. Gate: same as average load. Reference request: average load (5 min).

job.name: Test patterns (any URL): 07 recovery after the spike

jobs.name: Test patterns (any URL): 08 soak (1 hour at 60%)
jobs.notes: Step 8 of 10. One hour of steady load. Finds leaks and slow decay in memory, connections, file descriptors, disk, log volume and cache churn. Watch the resource graphs: any line that climbs and never flattens is a finding. Gate: at most 0.5% errors. Reference request: average load (5 min).

job.name: Test patterns (any URL): 08 soak (1 hour at 60%)

jobs.name: Test patterns (any URL): 09 breakpoint (find the ceiling)
jobs.notes: Step 9 of 10. Ramps to twenty times average over 20 minutes. Stop it when errors pass about 5%: the rate at that moment is your ceiling, and ceiling divided by peak is your capacity margin. Use a production-like environment, never production. Reference request: average load (5 min).

job.name: Test patterns (any URL): 09 breakpoint (find the ceiling)

jobs.name: Test patterns (any URL): 10 resilience window (failover / deploy)
jobs.notes: Step 10 of 10. Average load for 15 minutes. About 5 minutes in, cause the event you are testing: kill a pod or node, fail over the database, roll out a new version, drain a zone. Errors in the window are your real availability loss. Gate: at most 1% errors overall; read the time series for how long the dip lasted. Reference request: average load (5 min).

job.name: Test patterns (any URL): 10 resilience window (failover / deploy)

jobs.name: Test patterns (any URL): no keep-alive (new connection per request)
jobs.notes: Sends Connection: close, so every request pays for a new TCP and TLS handshake: the cost for clients that do not reuse connections (scripts, some mobile SDKs, health checkers). Shows load balancer and TLS termination limits. Reference request: average load (5 min).

job.name: Test patterns (any URL): no keep-alive (new connection per request)

jobs.name: Test patterns (any URL): crawler traffic (Googlebot user agent)
jobs.notes: Same request identified as a search crawler. Tests WAF and bot-management rules and whether crawlers get cached or origin responses. Crawlers can easily be a third of all traffic. Reference request: average load (5 min).

job.name: Test patterns (any URL): crawler traffic (Googlebot user agent)

jobs.name: Test patterns (any URL): large cookies (~4 KB header)
jobs.notes: Adds a 4 KB Cookie header, like a logged-in user with many tracking cookies. Proxies and servers reject headers around 8 KB, so this shows how close you are to that limit. Reference request: average load (5 min).

job.name: Test patterns (any URL): large cookies (~4 KB header)

jobs.name: Test patterns (any URL): uptime monitors (HEAD from many locations)
jobs.notes: A fleet of synthetic monitors checking the URL with HEAD requests every 30 seconds from 20 locations, plus load balancer probes. Cheap each, constant in total. Reference request: average load (5 min).

job.name: Test patterns (any URL): uptime monitors (HEAD from many locations)
